status: Primary-source research and source inspection; no new rendering experiment

sources.title: Enhanced Sphere Tracing
sources.access: Read the authored paper through a PDF mirror; publisher item access returned 403.
sources.supports: Overlap-checked fixed relaxation with ordinary fallback. Additional state, branches and rejected queries can offset query-count gains.
sources.cubey_inference: Use only the checked-stepping mechanism initially. Exclude screen-space forced hits, changed secondary offsets, hit smoothing and assumptions that the entire model is convex.

sources.title: Accelerating Sphere Tracing
sources.access: Publisher abstract and author-PDF indexed first page; this pass does not claim full algorithm qualification.
sources.supports: Locally planar step prediction with relaxation, and a separate multiresolution contribution.
sources.cubey_inference: Relevant alternate predictor for oblique surfaces. Defer an additional predictor and omit multiresolution from this fixed-quality comparison.

sources.title: Automatic Step Size Relaxation in Sphere Tracing
sources.access: Publisher paper search-indexed; direct paper retrieval returned 403. Detailed inspection uses the author implementation below.
sources.supports: The implementation compares fixed, planar and adaptive prediction. Adaptive state uses a smoothed accepted-sample slope and a conservative reset after a failed overlap test.
sources.cubey_inference: Inside exits, root coverage, cached-bound resets, finite progress, first-hit coverage and numerical guard need an independent port. Endpoint residual and the donor's one-sided termination are insufficient.

sources.title: Segment Tracing Using Local Lipschitz Bounds
sources.authors: Eric Galin, Eric Guérin, Axel Paris and Adrien Peytavie

files.inspection: Downloaded identity only; no algorithm claim depends on this file.

sources.access: Read author project abstract, repository README and relevant primitive/recursive segment-bound routines. README says this code reproduces only some results and differs from the paper's scene implementation.
sources.supports: Certified bounds over a segment require more information than sampled field values. The inspected implementation computes directional primitive bounds and combines bounds recursively.
sources.cubey_inference: Cubey would need a bound evaluator for its own primitives and operators. Defer that additional evaluator until checked point-sample relaxation is assessed.

sources.title: Lipschitz Pruning: Hierarchical Simplification of Primitive-Based SDFs
sources.access: Read authored PDF, including the distinction between exact local programs and far constants, and section 6.1.
sources.supports: Hierarchical pruning preserves exact local values, while far constants are lower bounds. Section 6.1 explicitly leaves sparse adaptive partitioning and partial updates as future work.
sources.cubey_inference: An active-parent-only child level is a new Cubey extension. Its reference count, construction cost, publication behavior and performance need independent qualification.

limits: No literature speedup is used as a Cubey forecast.
Historical workload counts are not a current optimized-path GPU cost breakdown.
Sparse child capacities are scenarios, not sampled or built child programs.
Research-code inspection is not native renderer qualification or automatic adoption.
